gap: No result ChatGPT got states that two sensors can both be native 3840 × 2160 and still differ 1.9× in light-collecting area per pixel (Sony IMX678, type 1/1.8, 2.0 µm, STARVIS 2, against Sony IMX415, type 1/2.8, 1.45 µm, first-generation STARVIS), nor Sony's own statement that DOL HDR blurs the outline of a fast-moving target while Clear HDR does not.
standout_why: Compared against Product Bible, RoadGearLab, Tony Reviews Things, Pacific Parts Dept and DashCamTalk's best list (all opened 2026-11-26). RoadGearLab already has native against upscaled 4K, the IMX678's size ('1/1.8-inch ... 8.29MP effective'), bitrates and GB per hour. Pacific Parts Dept has the upscaling point and the U3 card. None names the IMX415 as the smaller native-4K sensor, gives a pixel size, or explains HDR motion artifacts. Rivals therefore hold part of the sensor story (hence 2, not 3).
decides: It confirms an IMX678 camera as the pick for night plate detail (VIOFO A119M Pro front-only, 70mai A810S with a rear camera). Our Botslab G980H 4K + 2K is native 4K on the front channel but uses the smaller IMX415, and Android Authority's reviewer found plates hard to read at night, so it is honestly the cheaper daylight-4K pick, not the overall winner. Our Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K + 2.5K would compete on sensor terms, but I could not re-read its IMX678 claim on Vantrue's page today.

findings.source_title: Sony Semiconductor Solutions: Image Sensor for Security Camera lineup
findings.note: Sony's lineup page gives image size and aspect ratio only. Pixel size and effective pixels are in Sony's flyers, which I could not read (encrypted PDF).

findings.label: Pixel size and effective resolution of the two native-4K sensors
findings.source_title: e-con Systems: Sony IMX415 vs IMX715 vs IMX678 (Prabu Kumar, 2026-04-29, updated 2026-05-06)
findings.note: Named third-party source (a camera-module maker), not Sony. Arithmetic: 2.0² = 4.00 µm² against 1.45² = 2.10 µm², so 1.90× the area per pixel on the IMX678. Both sensors fill 3840 × 2160 without interpolation. Prabu Kumar calls the IMX678 'the preferred choice for low-light AI vision systems' because of 'its larger pixel architecture and STARVIS 2 technology'.

findings.label: HDR modes each sensor supports
findings.value: IMX415: multi-exposure + DOL HDR; IMX678: DOL HDR + Clear HDR
findings.source_title: e-con Systems: Sony IMX415 vs IMX715 vs IMX678 (Prabu Kumar)
findings.note: This is what the sensor supports; which mode a given dash cam's firmware uses is not stated here. The same article says STARVIS 2 has 'a wide dynamic range advantage exceeding 8 dB over STARVIS'.

findings.label: Why HDR can smear a moving plate, in Sony's words
findings.value: DOL HDR: 'this can cause some artifacts, such as a blurred outline and chromatic aberration, if the target is in fast motion'. Clear HDR 'has the advantage of delivering images of a moving target without chromatic aberration'
findings.source_title: Sony Semiconductor Solutions: Security camera image sensor technology (STARVIS / STARVIS 2)
findings.note: Sony explains that DOL takes two exposures in succession with a short time gap, while Clear HDR captures both images at the same time. Sony also defines STARVIS as sensitivity of at least 2,000 mV/µm² (colour product, 706 cd/m² light source).

findings.label: Image sensor and channels, per Botslab's specification page
findings.value: 'Powered by the Sony IMX 415 sensor'; video resolution '4K + 2K' (2-channel: front + rear); angle of view 170° + 150°; '24/7 Parking Mode: ✓ (Hard wire kit needed)'; 'Includes a 64GB MicroSD card'
findings.note: The page does not say which camera has the IMX415, and gives no frame rate, aperture, codec or card maximum.

findings.label: Night plate legibility, named reviewer
findings.value: Daylight: 4K front 'excellent for capturing finer details like license plates'. Night or highway speed: 'reading license plates can be difficult'; 'Low-light video can be poor'; 'The camera lacks HDR or a dedicated night mode'. One hour of front 4K 'will consume around 13GB'
findings.source_title: Android Authority: Botslab G980H review (Bogdan Petrovan, 2024-12-24)
findings.note: The unit reviewed had a 1080p rear camera, not the 2K rear of the bundle we link, and the review is from 2024. Its spec table lists the IMX415 for the front camera. Arithmetic: 13 GB/hour ≈ 29 Mb/s.
